sections.title: Benefits and getting the go-ahead
sections.text: ACOG advises that many people with uncomplicated pregnancies can continue or start suitable aerobic and strength-conditioning activity. Talk about exercise with your obstetric healthcare professional, especially if you’re starting a new routine or have complications. They can tell you whether your pregnancy is medically uncomplicated. TrainUp can’t.

sections.title: Adapt as things change
sections.text: Your balance, heat tolerance, breathing comfort and the movements you prefer may change through pregnancy. Choose comfortable activities. Avoid overheating, activities with a real risk of falls or collisions, and positions that make you dizzy. If you exercised a lot before, you may keep up some demanding activity with clinical guidance, since pregnancy doesn’t automatically mean total rest.

sections.title: Warning signs
sections.text: Stop exercising and contact your obstetric clinician if you have vaginal bleeding, fluid leaking, chest pain, dizziness, calf pain or swelling, painful contractions or unusual breathlessness. Emergency symptoms need urgent care. Don’t try to work around pregnancy-specific symptoms by swapping exercises.

sections.title: After childbirth
sections.text: When you can return to exercise depends on the delivery, your recovery, pelvic-floor symptoms and other personal factors. Easy walking may be fine for some people. Persistent pain, leaking, heaviness or other problems need a professional review, and no fixed timeline fits everyone. TrainUp doesn’t build pregnancy, pelvic-floor or post-surgery programs.
